subject: software clocks, counters and why rebooting works
title: What If You Never Restarted Your Computer?

scenes.text: What if you never restarted your computer? Its clock, not its hardware, would betray you first.
scenes.keywords: computer screen glowing in dark room

scenes.text: Over days, leaky programs hold on to memory they never give back, and everything slows.
After forty-nine point seven days, some old Windows ninety-five machines simply froze. A millisecond counter ran out of room.
After a hundred hours, one missile-defence computer ran a third of a second slow, aiming about seven hundred metres off.
A Boeing seven eight seven powered for two hundred forty-eight days straight could lose all electrical power.
So the oldest tech-support advice is real engineering. Turning it off and on again sets the clock back to zero.

description:
What if you never restarted your computer? Some Windows 95 and 98 systems stopped responding after exactly 49.7 days of continuous running, and a 2015 FAA directive warned that a Boeing 787 left powered for 248 days could lose all AC power because a software counter overflowed.
The US GAO found a Patriot battery's clock had drifted about 0.34 seconds after 100 hours, shifting its tracking gate by about 687 metres; rebooting reset it.
What should we run through next?
